alteration_systems.description: Hydrothermal alteration mineral assemblages used to vector toward gold ore zones

sericitization.indicator: Green-white color change in hand specimen
sericitization.spatial_relationship_to_ore: Form phyllic/sericitic alteration shell immediately surrounding ore zones; replaces feldspars and mafic minerals
sericitization.exploration_significance: Primary vectoring tool; presence indicates proximity to hydrothermal center. Maps the phyllic alteration zone that typically encloses higher-grade mineralization.
sericitization.field_identification: Soft, pale green to white rock; feldspars completely replaced; feels greasy

silicification.indicator: Hard, resistant outcrops; stands positive in relief
silicification.spatial_relationship_to_ore: May be directly coincident with ore (jasperoid replacement in Carlin systems) or proximal to vein systems in epithermal deposits
silicification.exploration_significance: Silica flooding indicates intense hydrothermal activity. In epithermal systems, chalcedony textures record boiling events critical for gold precipitation.
silicification.key_mineral_ratios: Quartz polymorph (chalcedony vs. crystalline) indicates temperature of formation
silicification.field_identification: Very hard, rings when struck; may be white, grey, or red (jasperoid); resistant to weathering

carbonatization.indicator: Brown weathering; rusty staining on outcrop surfaces
carbonatization.spatial_relationship_to_ore: Forms distal halo around gold-bearing shear zones; ankerite preferentially associated with higher-grade zones in orogenic systems
carbonatization.exploration_significance: Widest alteration halo of most orogenic systems; detectable in soil geochemistry as elevated CO2. Siderite-ankerite ratio may vector toward ore.
carbonatization.key_mineral_ratios: Ankerite:calcite ratio increases toward higher temperature conditions near ore
carbonatization.field_identification: Calcite fizzes with HCl (cold); ankerite fizzes weakly with warm HCl; siderite does not fizz and has brown color

chloritization.indicator: Dark green color; soft, planar cleavage
chloritization.spatial_relationship_to_ore: Distal propylitic alteration halo; forms broad zone surrounding more intense alteration
chloritization.exploration_significance: Maps the outermost expression of hydrothermal system; useful for identifying large-scale fluid pathways and structural controls on mineralization.
chloritization.key_mineral_ratios: Chlorite composition (Mg/Fe ratio) changes systematically with temperature toward ore
chloritization.field_identification: Very soft, dark green; easily scratched with fingernail; platy cleavage

argillic.indicator: Pale, soft zones; clay-rich; swelling when wet
argillic.spatial_relationship_to_ore: Intermediate argillic zone between phyllic and propylitic; advanced argillic forms above high-sulfidation ore bodies
argillic.exploration_significance: Advanced argillic (pyrophyllite, alunite, dickite) caps high-sulfidation deposits. In Carlin systems, clay alteration maps permeable host rocks.
argillic.key_mineral_ratios: Kaolinite:smectite ratio indicates acid intensity; advanced argillic minerals indicate pH <3
argillic.field_identification: Sticky when wet; white to pale grey; powdery when dry; swells noticeably

potassic.spatial_relationship_to_ore: Deepest alteration zone; directly associated with highest-grade copper-gold mineralization in porphyry systems
potassic.exploration_significance: Core of porphyry systems; presence indicates deep erosion level. Magnetite content aids magnetic survey targeting. K-feldspar veining (A/B veins) marks productive zones.
potassic.key_mineral_ratios: Secondary biotite:magnetite ratio indicates redox conditions and ore potential
potassic.field_identification: Pink to dark brown; K-feldspar has distinctive pink color; secondary biotite is black, platy, and associated with magnetite

structural_geology.description: Structural controls on gold mineralization — the geometric and kinematic framework that localizes ore bodies

characteristics.kinematics: Ductile to brittle-ductile; sinistral or dextral reverse

shear_zones.orientation: Typically NW-SE or NE-SW trending; subparallel to regional fabric

dilation_zones.description: Areas of extension within transpressional shear zones where gold precipitates
dilation_zones.ore_body_shape: Lenticular, pod-like; elongated parallel to shear; may have significant down-plunge extent

fault_valley_systems.description: Topographic depressions along major shear zones due to preferential weathering of altered rock
fault_valley_systems.exploration_significance: Easily mappable from satellite imagery; provides first-order targeting for orogenic gold
fault_valley_systems.typical_expression: Linear valleys with stream drainage, alluvial gold anomalies, and weathered bedrock exposures

exploration_targets: Saddle reefs at fold hinges within shears

saddle_reefs.description: Gold-bearing quartz veins that form in low-pressure zones at fold hinges
saddle_reefs.geometry: Lensoidal veins thickening at hinge, thinning along limbs
saddle_reefs.host_structures: Antiform hinges in interbedded competent/incompetent sequences

limb_deposits.description: Gold mineralization along fold limbs where bedding-parallel faults serve as fluid conduits
limb_deposits.ore_body_shape: Tabular, following bedding; may be repeated by folding

anticline_traps.description: Anticlinal crests trap gold-bearing fluids due to pressure gradients and structural permeability
trapping_mechanisms: Convergence of fluid pathways from limbs
anticline_traps.exploration_significance: Highly predictable geometry; drill targets at fold crest projections

cross_structure_targets.description: Where two fault sets intersect, enhanced permeability creates fluid focusing and gold precipitation
cross_structure_targets.ore_body_shape: Pipe-like or stockwork zones at intersection point
cross_structure_targets.exploration_significance: Prioritize drilling at mapped fault intersections; often overlooked in early-stage exploration

jog_zones.description: En echelon step-over zones between fault segments where extension creates dilation
jog_zones.kinematics: Extensional jogs in transtension; compressional in transpression
jog_zones.ore_body_geometry: Rhombohedral or lensoidal pods at jog
jog_zones.exploration_significance: High-grade pods; may be discrete and require tight drill spacing

banded_iron_formation.description: BIF-hosted gold deposits where iron-rich sediments provide a chemical trap for gold
banded_iron_formation.host_rock: Banded iron formation (hematite, magnetite, jasper, chert)
banded_iron_formation.chemical_trapping_mechanism: Sulfidation of iron-rich layers by H2S-bearing fluids precipitates gold with pyrite and pyrrhotite
banded_iron_formation.alteration_style: Silica flooding, carbonate alteration, sulfidation of magnetite to pyrrhotite
banded_iron_formation.ore_body_shape: Tabular, conformable with BIF; may extend along strike for kilometers

conglomerate_hosted.description: Witwatersrand-style paleoplacer deposits where gold is concentrated in conglomeratic horizons
conglomerate_hosted.deposition_type: Paleoplacer (detrital gold in ancient fluvial sediments)
conglomerate_hosted.ore_body_shape: Tabular, following paleochannel geometry; multi-kilometer strike
conglomerate_hosted.gold_association: Detrital gold grains in carbon seams; secondary enrichment by diagenesis and metamorphism
conglomerate_hosted.exploration_significance: Identify paleochannel systems from sedimentology; follow carbonaceous horizons. Resistant conglomerate bands form ridges useful for mapping.
